title: Tenant Quotas & LangChain Adapter Evaluation - SparrowGate
summary: Initial integration discovery focused on multi-tenant quotas, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter patterns, and a lightweight gateway/proxy approach. AtlasWorks is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for production; primary constraints are per-tenant rate limits, SSO/KMS, and token-level observability. SE follow-up to provide adapter example and quota enforcement patterns; security team to get SOC2 docs.
next_steps: Ethan to share LangChain adapter example repo and config snippets (by 2028-01-20)
Maya to send SOC2/ISO and network diagrams (by 2028-01-19)
Schedule SE-led latency/cost bench with sample workload (week of 2028-01-23)
Customer to provide expected qps and concurrent sessions for pilot (by 2028-01-22)
action_items: Ethan Brooks (SE): Create and share LangChain + LlamaIndex adapter example that shows token accounting and per-tenant header propagation - due 2028-01-20
Maya Patel (AE): Send SOC2/ISO overview, KMS integration notes, and pricing ballpark - due 2028-01-19
Priya Nair (CTO): Share tenant sizing spreadsheet (expected daily tokens, top 10 tenants) - due 2028-01-22
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-01-17 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood SE), Priya (AtlasWorks CTO), Ben (AtlasWorks Platform), Samir (AtlasWorks Security)

00:00:02 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we got Priya, Ben, Samir?
00:00:10 Priya (CTO): Yep hi, thanks. Sorry about the time change, east coast afternoon here.
00:00:15 Ben (Platform): Morning all.
00:00:20 Maya: Cool. Intent for today is to understand AtlasWorks' integration needs: multi-tenant quotas, LangChain/LlamaIndex usage, and what gateway or proxy approach fits best. Ethan will do the deep technical bits.
00:00:34 Ethan (SE): Hi, quick note — sorry if audio is fuzzy, I'm on a hotspot. What I'd like to get to is an example flow: client request -> gateway -> Redwood hosted/dedicated -> adapter back to LangChain/LlamaIndex or direct SDK. Also understand your SLOs.
00:00:52 Priya: Perfect. Background: we host a conversational assistant for multiple customers on shared infra. Each tenant has very different usage profiles — some bursty enterprise tenants, some low-volume startups. We want to enforce per-tenant quotas and have exact chargebacks by token.
00:01:10 Samir (Security): And we have SOC2 requirements, log retention for three years, KMS for key control, and SSO via SAML. So any hosted option needs to show compliance posture.
00:01:22 Maya: Understood. Two quick clarifications: are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or private? And do you use LangChain or LlamaIndex in prod now?
00:01:31 Priya: We're currently prototyping with LangChain in a few services and a couple connectors use LlamaIndex for doc retrieval. We want the ability to move between hosted for dev and dedicated for production later.
00:01:44 Ben: Also, we have an existing ingress gateway called SparrowGate — it's our sidecar/edge proxy for incoming webhooks. We were thinking to either integrate Redwood as a backend from SparrowGate or run a small proxy to add tenant headers, quotas, and batching.
00:01:58 Ethan: Good context. Two patterns we see: 1) Gateway-forwarding: SparrowGate forwards requests with a tenant-id header to Redwood's hosted API, Redwood handles token accounting and returns results, and SparrowGate enforces pre-check quotas. 2) Sidecar/proxy: run a small Redwood-aware proxy that does local rate limiting, batching and sticky sessions and then calls Redwood Dedicated/private endpoints. Which is attractive depends on latency and data isolation needs.
00:02:21 Ben: Latency is important — p95 needs to be under 600ms for short assistant queries. For longer generation we can tolerate more but want stable tail latency. Burst tolerance required for a few enterprise tenants.
00:02:33 Lina (SE): For p95 under 600ms, Dedicated or Private generally better, though hosted can fit if you use smaller model variants, caching and prefix KV cache. Also batching increases throughput but raises tail latency unless we use continuous batching with latency SLOs.
00:02:50 Priya: Can Redwood track tokens per tenant? We need exact numbers for billing our customers.
00:02:55 Ethan: Yes — token-level accounting is supported. We can propagate a tenant header or an x-customer-id. We record token counts and provide per-API-key breakdowns in the dashboard and in telemetry hooks. Small caveat — if you're routing through a shared API key you'll need to pass a tenant metadata header to attribute usage server-side.
00:03:14 Samir: About logs — do you provide audit logs with full request/response metadata? We can't send PII in logs so need redaction guidance.
00:03:21 Maya: We provide audit logs and structured request traces. You can configure payload redaction, and we support KMS (bring-your-own) so you control keys for encryption at rest. We'll send the SOC2 docs after this call.
00:03:35 Ben: For adapter libraries: we're mostly on LangChain 0.0x and some newer services using LlamaIndex. Do you have official SDK adapters or community ones?
00:03:45 Ethan: We have official SDKs in Python, Node, and a sample LangChain adapter repo. LlamaIndex connectors often work via the same SDK but sometimes need a small shim. We'll share a sample repo that shows both patterns: direct SDK usage and a LangChain agent adapter.
00:04:00 Priya: Example code would be huge. Could you include token accounting hooks so we can see where to intercept for billing?
00:04:07 Ethan: Absolutely. We'll show the call patterns and where Redwood emits token counts. Also example of propagating tenant-id in headers and mapping that to our per-key billing.
00:04:18 Ben: On quotas — can Redwood enforce per-tenant quotas at the gateway layer? Like daily tokens per-tenant, concurrent request caps, and rate per second.
00:04:27 Lina: Yes. There are several enforcement points: a) client-side via SparrowGate pre-checks b) Redwood ingress level with per-api-key or per-tenant quotas (token-based, request-based) c) Dedicated layer with isolation using reserved capacity and sharded pools. For hosted, we recommend a hybrid: enforce a soft quota at the gateway and hard limits at Redwood.
00:04:48 Samir: If we do soft quota at SparrowGate and hard limit at Redwood, what happens on denial — what response codes, backoff semantics? We need predictable behavior for the client app.
00:05:00 Ethan: Redwood returns 429 with a structured JSON error when a hard quota is hit. We can include retry-after headers. For soft quota you can implement leaky bucket in SparrowGate to smooth bursts and only call Redwood when under the soft threshold.
00:05:12 Priya: How about canary rollouts and model version pinning? We want to test new model variants with 5% traffic and fallback logic if latency or quality regressions occur.
00:05:21 Maya: Rollouts are supported — you can pin model versions per route and do canaries, A/B tests, automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency SLOs break. The console exposes per-model metrics and quality deltas when you upload eval prompt sets.
00:05:33 Ben: Observability hooks — we use Datadog and open-telemetry already. Can Redwood forward traces or provide distributed tracing IDs?
00:05:42 Ethan: We emit tracing headers (W3C traceparent) and can forward traces to your OTLP collector, or you can pull the telemetry via an API. We also provide detailed token-level cost events and per-request latency breakdowns that you can ingest into Datadog.
00:05:55 Samir: Are the telemetry hooks synchronous? We can't block request path waiting for a push to external telemetry during production traffic.
00:06:02 Ethan: No, telemetry emission is async — it's batched and pushed to your collector. For critical audit logs we offer a sync write path to your Kinesis/SQS if you choose dedicated/private.
00:06:14 Priya: Regarding proxy approach — what's the recommended footprint for a sidecar? We don't want large memory/CPU on our app nodes.
00:06:22 Lina: A lightweight sidecar is possible — usually a small Go binary that signs requests, enforces tenant quotas locally and does very small LRU caching for prefix hits. Batching and pooling can be offloaded to a central proxy cluster if you prefer.
00:06:35 Ben: We were worried about KV cache semantics. If we use LlamaIndex and Redis for embeddings cache, does Redwood's KV cache conflict? Will caching cause stale context problems?
00:06:45 Ethan: Redwood's prefix/KV cache is at the inference layer for key/value caches of past tokens and small prompt prefixes. For embeddings caches, you can keep Redis as your retrieval layer. We'll document best practices: keep retrieval caches and inference caches separate, invalidate on content updates, and version keys with tenant ids.
00:07:03 Priya: Could you walk through a sample HTTP flow end-to-end? Let's say user sends a query, LangChain invokes then calls Redwood.
00:07:10 Ethan: Sure. Timestamp 00:07:12 - User -> SparrowGate (auth, tenant-id) -> SparrowGate decides to call Redwood hosted API with Authorization: Bearer <redwood-api-key> and X-Tenant-Id: tenant-123. Redwood receives, maps token usage to tenant-123, checks quota. If under threshold, it forwards to model runtime (or cached response), returns tokens-used and model-output. SparrowGate records the response time and token count, increments its internal counters for soft quota, returns to user. If quota exceeded, Redwood replies 429 and SparrowGate surfaces user-friendly error with retry logic.
00:07:49 Ben: Okay so tenant mapping is straightforward. How about if multiple services call Redwood with the same API key?
00:07:55 Ethan: Then you must pass tenant-id with each request and we will attribute usage accordingly. If you can't, use per-tenant API keys to simplify billing.
00:08:05 Samir: Security question — network connectivity for private deployment: do you need to open inbound ports? We prefer outbound-only egress.
00:08:12 Maya: For Redwood Private (VPC), we can set up an outbound-only egress tunnel in many cases. On-prem package can be air-gapped but will require specific network setup. We'll capture your exact firewall constraints in the follow-up questionnaire.
00:08:25 Priya: What about data residency? Some tenants want EU-only hosting.
00:08:29 Maya: You can route tenant traffic to regional deployments or pin tenant to a region. For hosted we have regions in NA/EU/APAC; Dedicated and Private give you more control.
00:08:38 Ben: Pricing: high-level — hosted per-token but we need examples for heavy tenants.
00:08:43 Maya: We'll send pricing bands — for high-volume tenants we recommend Dedicated reserved pools which reduce unit cost and provide predictable latency.
00:08:51 Priya: For pilot, we want to start with 2 tenants: one enterprise (burst) and one small. We'll need a pilot that captures telemetry, quota enforcement, and billing.
00:08:59 Maya: Great. Proposed pilot: 2-week integration, Redwood provides a LangChain adapter example, AtlasWorks routes 2 tenants through SparrowGate -> Redwood hosted, set soft quotas at gateway and hard quotas with Redwood. We'll run bench tests for latency and token accounting.
00:09:13 Ben: Sounds good. Any known gaps?
00:09:17 Ethan: A few gotchas to watch: 1) If you rely on LlamaIndex incremental indexing, ensure your embedder calls are counted and properly attributed. 2) Some community LangChain agents do their own retries — make sure those retries don't double-count tokens. 3) For heavy prefix caching, pre-warm KV cache to avoid cold miss latency.
00:09:34 Priya: That retry double-counting sounds dangerous. How to avoid it?
00:09:38 Ethan: Best practice: idempotency keys and dedupe at SparrowGate; also Redwood can return idempotency tokens from earlier calls if you surface them; we'll share patterns.
00:09:49 Samir: One last security - we need threat modeling for the sidecar approach. Who can we send the model to for review?
00:09:56 Maya: We'll loop in our security contact; I'll include Lina and our compliance lead in the SOC2 packet. We'll also set up a separate security deep-dive with your team.
00:10:06 Priya: Great. Anything else on observability?
00:10:09 Ben: We need per-tenant dashboards and per-route latency histograms; sampling for traces to keep costs down.
00:10:15 Ethan: Dashboarding is per-route/per-key and you can export metrics. We support sampling rules for traces and will include cost events only at a desired sampling rate if you want to avoid data volume.
00:10:26 Priya: Thanks. Can you include an example of how token-level events look in Datadog? We want to wire straight into our billing pipeline.
00:10:33 Ethan: We'll provide a snippet — event format: tenant_id, request_id, tokens_input, tokens_output, model, latency_ms.
00:10:41 Maya: Ok, recapping next steps — Ethan share repo and adapter example; Maya share SOC2 and pricing; AtlasWorks share tenant sizing. We'll schedule bench week of 23rd.
00:10:53 Priya: Sounds good.
00:10:55 Ben: Quick note — we'll also explore ModelHostX pricing to compare.
00:11:00 Maya: Noted.
00:11:03 (longer technical side convo omitted)
00:30:12 Ethan: Back to the adapter specifics — the LangChain sample will include a small middleware to add X-Tenant-Id and idempotency-key, plus a wrapper that extracts token counts from Redwood's response and emits to a local Kafka topic for billing.
00:30:30 Ben: That Kafka emission is interesting. Do you recommend pushing raw events or aggregated counts?
00:30:36 Ethan: For billing accuracy, raw per-request events are best; then you can aggregate daily. But if bandwidth matters, aggregate at SparrowGate and only send summaries.
00:30:48 Priya: For the pilot we want raw events but with PII redaction.
00:30:53 Samir: We'll add an ACL and schema to make sure nothing sensitive flows.
00:31:00 Maya: I'll include log redaction docs.
00:31:05 (some crosstalk)
00:41:02 Maya: Any blockers on scheduling the bench?
00:41:06 Ben: We need to confirm hardware and tenants but should be fine.
00:41:10 Priya: We'll send the spreadsheet by Monday the 22nd.
00:41:13 Maya: Great. Thanks everyone.
00:41:18 Priya: Thanks.
00:41:21 Maya: End.

Notes: some transcription artifacts — "K V cash" heard once in call (actually KV cache). Also SE audio glitch at 00:00:34. References: SparrowGate (customer internal gateway), LangChain, LlamaIndex. Shared artifacts mentioned: LangChain adapter repo link (to be shared), SOC2 and pricing docs.
